title: Motor Imagery vs Rest - Low-Cost EEG System
description: This dataset comprises electroencephalography (EEG) signals acquired from 10 naive participants using a low-cost consumer-grade EEG device during a motor imagery brain-computer interface protocol. Participants performed kinesthetic imagination of dominant-hand grasping movements and rest conditions across five protocol runs, with electromyography (EMG) recorded from the dominant hand for protocol validation. EEG signals were bandpass-filtered between 0.5 and 45 Hz using a 3rd-order Butterworth filter at a sampling rate of 125 Hz.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a low-cost consumer-grade device from 10 participants with no prior BCI experience. The protocol consisted of five runs: RUN0 involved real grasping movement for instruction and familiarization, while RUN1-RUN4 consisted of motor imagery (kinesthetic imagination of dominant-hand grasping) versus rest conditions. EMG signals from the dominant hand were recorded for protocol control. EEG signals were filtered with a 3rd-order Butterworth bandpass filter (0.5-45 Hz) during acquisition. Sampling rate was 125 Hz with 15 EEG channels using the 10-20 electrode placement scheme.
